messages:
yara: quick note — spinning up osmium14b (14B) int4 canary on small pool for longform QA. seeing OOMs when requests ask for >700 tokens, plus p95 jitter. drops and logs below.

thomas: can you paste the canary runtime config and the exact stderr?

yara: config: microbatch=1, batch=6, prefetch_window=180, prefetch_padding=0, max_new_tokens=1200. artifact: s3://redwood-bench/osmium14b/int4/contig-2026-04-02

yara: stderr snippet: ```RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory while allocating 1.3 GiB
slab_allocator: largest_free_chunk=680MB total_free=2.0GB
Backtrace: runtime/slab.cc:410 -> kv_store.cc:188 -> decoder.cc:92
Timeline: prefetch->kv_populate->attn_kv_alloc->decode```

su: largest_free_chunk vs total_free => fragmentation. With quant layouts that's common because many small allocations fragment the slab and block large contiguous allocs for long generations.

ben: short remediation experiments: (A) reduce prefetch_window to 48 + set prefetch_padding=32; (B) cap canary default max_new_tokens=512; (C) add compact-on-failure: attempt slab compaction for up to 150ms then retry, else soft-evict oldest KV pages up to 20%.

thomas: run (A)+(B) first — lower risk. if OOMs persist, try (C) behind feature flag. Also run eval sweep to check for truncation-related quality regressions (ROUGE/BERTScore).

yara: repro commands: `./run_canary.sh --model osmium14b --quant int4 --prefetch 180 --max_new 1200 --requests 800` => ~3 OOMs. Changing to `--prefetch 48 --prefetch_padding 32 --max_new 512` => 0 OOMs in 1k requests, p95 down ~12%, ROUGE-L delta -2.7 vs fp16.

ben: observation — lowering max_new_tokens reduces OOM surface but may hide longform quality issues. compact-on-failure avoids conservative truncation but costs a small latency hit. microbench with compact-on-failure (ff on) => p95 +3%, OOMs -> 0 for 2k run.

su: propose onboarding policy: for int4 variants set model_config defaults: max_new_tokens=512, prefetch_window<=64, prefetch_padding=32. expose `model_config.prefetch_strategy=adaptive` (base + request_len/8 capped by max_prefetch_bytes) for later tuning. enable compact-on-failure as feature flag for heavy workloads.

thomas: SGTM. create ticket with artifacts and evaluation plan.
jira-bot: Created ML-1810: "osmium14b-int4 onboarding: conservative defaults + contig-alloc fallback + adaptive prefetch"

yara: Plan: (1) roll canary with conservative defaults, (2) run 10k request sweep (summarization + longform QA) capturing p50/p95/p99, OOM count, ROUGE-L, BERTScore, n-gram repeat rate, cost/tokens, (3) if quality delta <=2 pts and compact-on-failure perf hit <=5%, consider enabling compact for canary pool.

ben: I'll prototype compact-on-failure PR and add telemetry (compact_attempts, reclaimed_bytes, soft_evictions). Gate it behind `runtime.feature.compact_on_alloc`.

yara: will post sweep artifacts and update ML-1810. short-term keep prod int4 defaults conservative. thanks team :thumbsup:
